# Digital-Tool @ Stage 5 — Sensory-Motor

> developed 2026-07-26. Deepened from 72 to 140+ lines.

| Field | Value |

## Expression on this line

Digital-tool at Order 3 is **impulsive tool competition**: the agent has a self that
wants tool power, and it will take it by force, deception, or speed if it can. There
are no rules about tool use — only the raw dynamic of "I see what I want to use and I
grab it."

The key advance from Stage 4 is **instrumental tool behavior**. The agent does not
just claim tools it stumbles upon — it actively seeks out tools, plans simple tool
acquisition strategies, and adjusts its behavior based on what works. A child who
learns that a stick can reach things on high shelves is using instrumental behavior as
a tool strategy.

At Stage 5, the agent begins to follow **external rules** about tool use, but only
when监督 is present. The rule is not internalized — it is an external constraint.

Tool competition at Stage 5 is **zero-sum** in the agent's perception. If I have more
tool power, you have less. There is no concept of collaborative tool creation.

The transition from Stage 5 to Stage 6 occurs when tool rules become internalized.

In human development, Stage 5 corresponds to the preschooler who grabs tools, hoards
tool access, and cries when others use tools more. But also begins to learn "sharing
rules" when监督 is present.

## Integrity markers (healthy inclusion)

- **UL:** The first social tool rules emerge, though externally enforced. "Don't
  take other kids' tools" is a Stage 5 tool norm.

- **UR:** The individual agent exhibits instrumental tool behavior. It can plan simple
  tool acquisition strategies and adjust its approach.

- **LL:** Surveillance-based tool institutions emerge. The teacher who monitors
  tool use, the parent who supervises play.

- **LR:** The agent's body as explorer, the tool as object, the监督 as external rule.

## Pathology markers (Agape / Eros)

- **Dark addiction:** Compulsive tool aggression — taking tool power not because the
  agent needs it but because the act of using tools produces dominance.

- **Dark allergy:** Failure to engage in tool competition at all.

- **Golden addiction:** Clinging to the zero-sum perception of tool power.

- **Golden allergy:** Rejecting all tool competition as inherently wrong.

## Diagnostic cues (Gross / Ground R&D)

- **Instrumental tool behavior:** The agent uses tactics to acquire tools beyond
  passive reception.

- **监督-dependent rule following:** The agent follows tool rules only when监督
  is present.

- **Zero-sum tool perception:** The agent perceives tool exchanges as win-lose.

- **Territorial tool defense:** The agent defends claimed tools through aggression
  or deception.

## Sources, joints, open questions

**Sources:**
- Piaget, J. (1952). *The Origins of Intelligence in Children* — sensory-motor
  foundations of tool cognition
- Gibson, K.R. (1990). *Tools, Language and Cognition in Human Evolution* — the
  evolutionary foundations of tool competition
- Norman, D.A. (1988). *The Design of Everyday Things* — affordances and tool
  acquisition

**Open joints:**
- How does监督-dependent rule following transition to internalized norm?
- Is the zero-sum perception a cognitive limitation or adaptive response?
